// R2 used to fire only where the call was written X.Run(...), so binding the
// method to a name first ran exactly the forbidden subtest and the gate said
// nothing. What is prohibited is the method, so the reference to it is the
// finding, whatever is done with the value afterwards.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

// stepper has nothing to do with quicktest. Its Run is bound to a name below
// exactly as the checker's is, and is not a violation.
type stepper struct{}

func (stepper) Run(name string, step func(int)) {}

func register(run func(string, func(*qt.C)) bool) {}

func TestRunBoundToAName(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	run := c.Run
	run("the method value is the same subtest", func(c *qt.C) {
		c.Assert(1, qt.Equals, 1)
	})
}

func TestRunAsAMethodExpression(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	(*qt.C).Run(c, "the method expression is the same subtest", func(c *qt.C) {
		c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
	})
}

func TestRunHandedToAHelper(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	register(c.Run)
}

func TestUnrelatedRunBoundToAName(t *testing.T) {
	var steps stepper

	run := steps.Run
	run("an unrelated runner is not a subtest", func(int) {})

	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Check(3, qt.Equals, 3)
}
